method: These7 exact original PNGs were actually viewed by agent through view_image after full-1 terminal. No edits, new browser, state changes or human observations.

images.name: training-overview
images.observation: Actual finalB G0 training has visible helmet/top/side, boots/ground ring, raised folds, distant wall and foreground layers. Full input log separately establishes planar eight-way movement and360-degree aiming.

images.name: player-behind-terminal
images.observation: Player is physically behind the terminal at the sampled foot-Y, terminal covers lower torso while head remains visible; nearby foreground folds are faded.

images.name: player-in-front-of-terminal
images.observation: Player has crossed the terminal foot-Y and is drawn in front of the terminal, without any camera/physics rule change.

images.name: foreground-fades-and-player-remains-readable
images.observation: Actual foreground tissue is translucent while the player body and foot location remain readable. This sampled crossing is not an all-frame no-occlusion assertion.

images.name: 1366x768-dpr1-pointer-hit
images.observation: At1366x768 DPR1, actual shot points to the target crosshair and a visibly reduced HP bar; outcome/coordinate details come from the attached actual-hit record.

images.name: 1920x1080-dpr2-pointer-hit
images.observation: At1920x1080 DPR2, actual shot/crosshair and target damage agree. Tool display downscaled3840x2160 to2048x1152, so no single-pixel claim is made.

images.name: 1100x700-dpr1.5-pointer-hit
images.observation: At1100x700 DPR1.5, actual crosshair lies on damaged target, HUD/tool row remain visible. This is a viewport/DPR check, not actual browser zoom.

limits: Actual movement/ray/collision facts rely on the completed read-only-snapshot/actual-DOM full cases, not still image inference alone.
No true browser zoom, native OS focus, new-player recognition or universal dense HUD readability conclusion.
